coverage.label: Saturday 18 July 2026, 0700 SGT → Sunday 19 July 2026, 0700 SGT

global.headline: FIRST US COMBAT DEATHS OF THE WAR: TWO TROOPS KILLED, ONE MISSING IN IRANIAN STRIKE ON JORDAN; IRAN DECLARES ITS MOU COMMITMENTS SUSPENDED AS AN ADVISER THREATENS 'COMPLETE DESTRUCTION'
summary: Iranian ballistic missiles hit Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti air base on Friday night, killing two US service members and leaving a third missing — the first American combat deaths of the war since an April truce, taking the US military death toll to 16. Four other Americans were medically evacuated and later discharged. The IRGC said it destroyed the base's command centre and hangars housing US MQ-9 Reaper drones; Jordan said its air defences intercepted most of the roughly ten missiles fired. CENTCOM responded with an eighth consecutive night of strikes that, for the first time this round, used fighter jets rather than only standoff weapons, reaching roughly 650km inland to Yazd in central Iran. Trump told Fox News the campaign would "continue until I say it's enough."

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharib Abadi said Washington had "violated and suspended all its commitments" under the Islamabad MOU and that Tehran had "likewise suspended all our own commitments" — the clearest declaration yet that the ceasefire framework signed in June no longer binds either side, though neither has filed a formal termination. Separately, Mohsen Rezaei, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader and a former IRGC commander-in-chief, warned on state TV that if strikes continue another "two or three days," Iran will move from retaliatory strikes to "offensive and complete destruction," saying "no political border will be safe" — a threat of uncertain authority given his advisory (not command) role and Mojtaba Khamenei's continued public absence, but one state broadcaster IRIB aired as a signal regardless.

Kuwait was hit for a second consecutive night — a power and water desalination plant caught fire and lost generation units, an army barracks was struck (several injured), and a Kuwait Petroleum Corp oil facility suffered "significant material damage"; Kuwait International Airport briefly suspended flights. The Gulf Cooperation Council's secretary-general said Iran's strikes on civilian sites in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan amount to "war crimes." Iran's Health Ministry said 50 people have been killed (5 women, 2 children) and 500+ injured since 6 July, with 12 of those deaths in the latest 24 hours alone. Brent crude rose above $87/barrel, its highest since June, up more than 14% for the week.
global.geopolitical: American blood on the ground for the first time since the truce collapsed removes Washington's main incentive for restraint just as Iran formally disavows the ceasefire framework and one of its own advisers threatens to abandon proportional retaliation altogether — a combination that leaves the war's next 48-72 hours looking far more dangerous than the seven nights that preceded them.
global.socioeconomic: Brent above $87 and climbing for a second straight week feeds directly into the same inflation channel already visible in Singapore's record COE premiums and Q3 electricity tariff, raising the stakes for how much further MAS tightens at its upcoming policy review.

global.headline: HUNGARY'S PRESIDENT AGREES TO STAND DOWN AFTER PARLIAMENT VOTES HIM OUT IN LATEST ANTI-ORBAN MOVE
summary: President Tamás Sulyok, an Orbán-era appointee, has agreed to leave office after Hungary's parliament passed a constitutional amendment on 13 July ending his term, with the move formalised this week ahead of his five-day deadline to sign. Prime Minister Péter Magyar's Tisza Party — which ended 16 years of Fidesz rule in April's landslide election and holds a two-thirds supermajority — had branded Sulyok a Fidesz "puppet" and "unworthy to embody the unity of the Hungarian nation," threatening impeachment if he refused to sign. The same amendment creates an office to investigate financial abuses under the Orbán government and imposes a 12-year term limit on lawmakers.
global.geopolitical: A rare peaceful, constitutional removal of an incumbent head of state completes Hungary's post-Orbán institutional turnover and signals Magyar intends to use his supermajority aggressively to dismantle Fidesz-era appointments rather than simply govern around them.
global.socioeconomic: No direct Singapore exposure, but continued Hungarian political consolidation is a data point for how quickly one of the EU's most Orbán-aligned governments can be unwound, relevant to Singapore's own reading of EU policy stability on trade and sanctions.

global.headline: UKRAINE'S DRONE STRIKES KILL EIGHT AT RUSSIAN WAREHOUSES IN DEADLIEST ATTACK ON RUSSIAN SOIL IN TWO YEARS, AS FEDOROV-OUSTER PROTESTS TURN ON TOP GENERAL SYRSKYI
summary: Ukrainian drones struck two Wildberries e-commerce warehouses — in Russia's Tambov and Moscow regions, 500-700km from the front line — killing eight people (seven at Kotovsk, one at Elektrostal) and injuring more than 50; President Zelensky said the sites supplied sanctioned components for drone and navigation-equipment production. It is the deadliest Ukrainian strike inside Russia in over two years, with preliminary damage estimated above 50 billion rubles and up to 15% of Wildberries' warehouse space affected.

At home, protests over Zelensky's dismissal of popular Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov have widened and sharpened, with demonstrators and veterans now directing anger at commander-in-chief Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi — the official Zelensky said Fedorov had unresolved friction with — rather than at Fedorov's replacement. The Air Force's deputy commander and other officials have resigned in protest, and analysts are increasingly framing the episode as Zelensky having inadvertently created a political rival during a sensitive wartime reshuffle.
global.geopolitical: A Ukraine simultaneously capable of its most damaging strike on Russian territory in two years and consumed by a domestic political crisis over its own military leadership is a harder partner for Western backers to read heading into any future ceasefire negotiation.
global.socioeconomic: None material for Singapore directly; continued volatility in Kyiv's wartime cabinet and expanding strikes on Russian logistics keep uncertainty elevated for European energy and defence planning alongside the Iran-driven oil shock.

global.headline: TOP GERMAN CONSERVATIVE JENS SPAHN RESIGNS AS CDU/CSU PARLIAMENTARY LEADER OVER US SURROGACY REVELATION
summary: Jens Spahn, leader of the CDU/CSU parliamentary group and a senior ally of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, resigned Friday after it emerged that he and his husband Daniel Funke had a child via a surrogate mother in the United States — a practice banned under German law. The controversy was sharpened by Spahn's own past public opposition to certain surrogacy models, which critics called hypocritical once his own arrangement became known. Merz, who had called on Spahn to step down, said the resignation was "the right one" and "unavoidable," adding that "credibility is the highest asset in politics."
global.geopolitical: Removes one of Merz's most prominent parliamentary lieutenants at a moment the CDU/CSU is managing a full domestic and European agenda, and reopens Germany's unresolved debate over its restrictive surrogacy law.
global.socioeconomic: None material for Singapore; a domestic German political resignation with no direct economic channel.

global.headline: SEVEN AMERICANS ARE FIRST TO USE NEW KENYA EBOLA QUARANTINE FACILITY, AS UGANDA PUSHES TO LIFT TRAVEL RESTRICTIONS AFTER LAST PATIENT DISCHARGED
summary: Seven American aid workers from Samaritan's Purse's Disaster Assistance Response Team, who had been responding to the DRC Ebola outbreak, became the first people to use a new US-built bio-isolation facility at a Kenyan air force base, undergoing a 21-day precautionary quarantine after one high-risk exposure among the group; none has shown symptoms. The facility is required under a US policy that Americans returning from DRC — or, more narrowly, certain travellers from Uganda and South Sudan — must spend three weeks in a third country before entering the US; an order extending the underlying entry suspension by 30 days was issued 13 July. Uganda, meanwhile, is pressing affected countries to lift their Ebola-related travel restrictions after discharging its last patient on 16 July, with a 42-day countdown now running before the outbreak can be formally declared over.
global.geopolitical: Highlights the gap between Uganda's on-the-ground progress against the outbreak and Washington's still-tightening entry restrictions, a friction point for US relations with African governments even as the DRC side of the outbreak continues to worsen.
global.socioeconomic: No direct Singapore exposure; Singapore's own S$2.5m WHO/Africa CDC pledge (14 Jul) remains the extent of its involvement, with no new funding development this window.

singapore.headline: OIL PATCHES SPOTTED OFF PULAU UBIN, SFA HELPS THREE FISH FARMS WITH CLEAN-UP
summary: The Singapore Food Agency said it is assisting three fish farms in the East Johor Strait affected by oil patches spotted near Pulau Ubin, supporting clean-up efforts and taking precautionary measures at the sites. SFA did not specify a source for the oil in the reports reviewed.
singapore.socioeconomic: A recurring East Johor Strait oil-fouling risk to Singapore's coastal fish farms, an aquaculture sector the government has been trying to expand as part of its "30 by 30" local food-production target.

singapore.headline: OVERSEAS GAMBLING SITE USED THREE SINGAPORE SHELL FIRMS TO COLLECT ILLEGAL WORLD CUP BETS
summary: GemBet, a Curaçao-based gambling site with a Singapore-facing URL, has been funnelling illegal World Cup betting deposits and payouts through three Singapore-registered companies — a manpower contracting firm, a cleaning-services company and a wholesale trading firm, all incorporated between March and May this year — with punters paying via PayNow or cryptocurrency into digital wallets. It follows a 6 July islandwide operation that saw 17 people arrested and more than $720,000 seized in a separate unlawful-remote-gambling crackdown. Individual bettors face fines up to $10,000 and up to six months' jail; operators and facilitators face fines up to $500,000 and up to seven years' jail.
singapore.socioeconomic: Illustrates how quickly-incorporated local shell companies are being used to launder World Cup betting funds during Singapore's tournament-period enforcement push, a vulnerability regulators are still working to close.

singapore.headline: DBS AND POSB LAUNCH $3 OFF EGGS AND RICE EVERY SATURDAY AS FIRST PHASE OF $10M COST-OF-LIVING SUPPORT
summary: DBS and POSB cardholders can get $3 off selected house-brand eggs and $3 off selected house-brand rice every Saturday from 18 July to 29 August at Sheng Siong and Giant supermarkets, with no minimum spend and one redemption per item per day while stocks last. It is the first phase of a S$10 million DBS support package for households managing living costs; the bank has said a further S$3 PayLah! cashback programme will follow from September, with details to come.
singapore.socioeconomic: A bank-funded grocery subsidy targeting two staples arrives as Singapore households continue to absorb record COE premiums and a record Q3 electricity tariff, part of the broader private and public cost-of-living relief push alongside the Aug 2026 GST Voucher payouts.

singapore.headline: CAT FOSTERERS TO BE ALLOWED UP TO SIX CATS IN HDB FLATS UNDER NEW PILOT SCHEME
summary: Approved cat fosterers will be allowed to keep up to six cats in HDB flats under a new pilot scheme, well above the standard two-cat limit for HDB households, aimed at supporting community efforts to shelter and rehome stray and abandoned cats.
singapore.socioeconomic: A modest regulatory carve-out that formalises informal fostering networks already operating in HDB estates, easing a bottleneck in Singapore's stray-cat management and rehoming pipeline.

singapore.headline: DRIVER ARRESTED FOR DRINK-DRIVING OVER FATAL HIT-AND-RUN NEAR SUNTEC CITY
summary: A 38-year-old man has been arrested for drink-driving and driving without due care causing death, after a 43-year-old man was fatally struck near Suntec City along Nicoll Highway in the early hours of 16 July; the driver is also being investigated for failing to stop after the accident. The victim's friends have appealed for witnesses and dashcam or CCTV footage to help establish what happened. Police investigations are ongoing.
singapore.socioeconomic: None material beyond standing road-safety enforcement.

word.definition: The formal rejection or giving-up of a right, claim, agreement, or course of action, especially one previously accepted as binding.
word.etymology: From Latin renuntiatio, from renuntiare ("to bring back word, protest against, renounce"), from re- ("back") + nuntiare ("to announce," from nuntius, "messenger"); entered English in the 15th century via Old French renunciation.
word.example: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister framed Tehran's suspension of the Islamabad MOU as a mutual renunciation of commitments rather than a unilateral collapse — even as the first American combat deaths of the war and an adviser's threat of "complete destruction" made the ceasefire's renunciation look far from theoretical.
